Index.title: Bharat Census 2027 Sahayak
Index.scheduleDesc: Below is the state-wise schedule for self-enumeration and survey dates. All dates are currently placeholders until officially published.

phases.title1: Phase 1: House Listing and Housing Census
phases.desc1: In this phase, data of all buildings, houses and amenities available in them will be collected. Based on this, the housing condition in India will be assessed.
phases.desc2: This is the main phase in which demographic, social and economic information of every person in the country will be obtained.
phases.list2_1: Name, age and gender of person
phases.list2_5: Mother tongue and other known languages

footer.gov: Government of India | Ministry of Home Affairs | Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, India
footer.demo: Bharat Census. This is a demo application and should not be considered an official government portal.

privacy.protectionContent: Your personal data is encrypted at rest and stored securely on sovereign servers. It is never shared with any third-party agencies.
privacy.legalContent: All data collection strictly abides by the Census Act, 1948, and the Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act, 2023. Confidentiality breaches are strictly punishable under law.
privacy.contactContent: If you have any concerns regarding data privacy, please reach out to the grievance officer at the Office of the Registrar General, India.

myths.myth1: Myth: Aadhaar number is mandatory for Census 2027.
myths.fact1: Fact: No Aadhaar is asked. It is completely optional.
myths.myth2: Myth: Religion is detected automatically from your name.
myths.fact2: Fact: Religion is strictly self-declared only.
myths.myth3: Myth: Data is stored outside of India.
myths.fact3: Fact: All data is stored on sovereign servers within India.
myths.myth4: Myth: Census data is shared with tax authorities.
myths.fact4: Fact: Census data is strictly confidential and not shared with tax authorities under the Census Act 1948.
myths.myth5: Myth: I have to show property papers to the enumerator.
myths.fact5: Fact: Enumerators will never ask for property papers or financial documents.
